environment.scope: Metadata snapshot outside measured stages. Exposed CPU model/MHz need not describe a dedicated host or sustained workload frequency. Cgroup root data is reported with proc_self_cgroup and is not assumed to be the effective quota. These fields do not establish IPC, memory bandwidth, cache misses or NUMA locality.

perf_probe.scope: User-space event availability probe on the true utility only; not a project measurement. No hardware counts from this probe may be attributed to a simulation phase.
perf_probe.stderr:
Error:
No supported events found.
Access to performance monitoring and observability operations is limited.
Consider adjusting /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid setting to open
access to performance monitoring and observability operations for processes
without CAP_PERFMON, CAP_SYS_PTRACE or CAP_SYS_ADMIN Linux capability.
More information can be found at 'Perf events and tool security' document:
https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/perf-security.html
perf_event_paranoid setting is 4:
  -1: Allow use of (almost) all events by all users
      Ignore mlock limit after perf_event_mlock_kb without CAP_IPC_LOCK
>= 0: Disallow raw and ftrace function tracepoint access
>= 1: Disallow CPU event access
>= 2: Disallow kernel profiling
To make the adjusted perf_event_paranoid setting permanent preserve it
in /etc/sysctl.conf (e.g. kernel.perf_event_paranoid = <setting>)

records.boundary_scope: Explicit Python wrappers count calls and perf_counter spans without cProfile. Inclusive spans overlap. Exclusive instrumented time subtracts only wrapped descendants and still includes unwrapped Python/native work and observer overhead; it is not pure Python interpreter time. Native scoring span includes conversion, worker startup/wait and computation. Wrappers are restored before state capture. Results must match plain state/RNG digests and call-count integrity gates. When the standalone encounter entry is present, protected entity/handler/manager methods are left untouched. Only its outer entry is wrapped and every human generation must return a non-None native result, ruling out observer-forced fallback. The entry span includes eligibility, packing, core execution and writeback. Separate eligibility and C ABI execution spans identify marshaling overhead without modifying any protected entity or handler method. Eligibility covers structural checks; batched finite-value checks are inside the remaining entry time, so compare the total entry span across revisions. Population, diversity and stagnation statistics may share batched path reads outside the encounter entry; their cost remains in the enclosing generation/evolution spans. Resident core sync/run/birth spans use the actual shared C binding table; the human case must use one persistent World for all generations. ResidentWorld spans include its Python adapter. All source identities and eligibility guards remain unchanged. Scalar C ABI conversion is included in its calling phase; no timer is subtracted.
